usage:
Run everything from /home/qzhao/render_demo.

1. Sprites (stills, GPU 7 only, about 13 s; writes assets/ui/*.png and sprites.json):
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 tools/blender/blender -b --factory-startup -P shots/s00_ui_sprites.py
   To render only some sprites: add `-- --only pill,chip,dots --samples 768`

2. Overlays (all 900 frames in about 8 s on 24 processes; writes renders/overlays/o_####.png):
   tools/venv/bin/python -I scripts/make_overlays.py
   Options:
   - `--frames 121-238,451` (or `1-900:10`) renders a subset with the same pixels as a full run
   - `--slug` adds "Illustrative · rendered with Cycles" (off by default)
   - `--sheet renders/review/overlays_sheet.png [--sheet-frames 25,61,...] [--sheet-bg auto|grey|final|preview]` writes the review sheet
   - `--fallback-sprites` tests the Pillow fallback pills
   - `--jobs N`, `--out DIR`
   Live values come from renders/meta/<id>.json. Any missing file, key or frame falls back to the storyboard section 4 formulas, and the run log says which source each value used.

3. Assembly:
   - Final deliverable: `tools/venv/bin/python -I scripts/assemble.py --mode final --master`
     Fails and lists the missing frames as ranges if any of the 900 frames are absent.
     Writes out/LaRenderer_opening.mp4, out/LaRenderer_opening_clean.mp4, out/LaRenderer_opening_master.mov, out/LaRenderer_opening_clean_master.mov, out/cuts.png and out/assembly.json.
   - Review build: `tools/venv/bin/python -I scripts/assemble.py --mode preview --allow-missing [--master]`
     Upscales the 960x540 preview frames with Lanczos and fills gaps with labelled placeholders. Writes the same file names under out/preview/.
   - Other flags: `--slug` (passed through to the overlays), `--skip-overlays` (reuse renders/overlays), `--no-encode`, `--jobs N`.
   - It always rebuilds the overlays first, then composites at 16 bit into renders/film_comp/ and renders/film_comp_clean/ (renders/film/ holds symlinks). It then encodes with tools/ffmpeg/ffmpeg: H.264 yuv420p, CRF 16, slow preset, error-diffusion dither, BT.709 matrix and tags; with --master also ProRes 422 HQ yuv422p10le with bt709 tags. Finally it runs the film QA checks: 900 frames, cuts on bar lines, no overlay pixel on the 2 frames before each cut, and the frame count of each encode.

4. QA (storyboard section 7). Mean |diff| is reported in /255 levels. Crops are X,Y,W,H in 1920x1080 film pixels and are scaled automatically for previews. Every run writes a heat-map to renders/qa/. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 over --max, 2 missing frames.
   - `tools/venv/bin/python -I scripts/qa_diff.py check s01-loop [--mode preview]` checks f195 against f135, limit 0.5.
   - `... qa_diff.py check s03-static --crop X,Y,W,H` checks consecutive frames f31-60, limit 1.
   - `... qa_diff.py check s04-hold` checks the centre 400x400 over f106-165.
   - `... qa_diff.py check s02-strip` checks f61-72.
   - `... qa_diff.py pair A.png B.png [--crop X,Y,W,H] [--max 0.5] [--heatmap out.png]`
   - `... qa_diff.py range <shot_id|folder> --frames 31-60 [--mode final|preview] [--prefix o_] [--crop ...] [--max 1] [--csv out.csv]`

I reviewed it at 1:1 and 3x and changed four things: square plates around the dots (shadow-catcher occlusion cut off by the sprite edge), a long dot shadow, a hard text clip while chips grow, and a chip undershoot that clipped "1×". Chip digits sit in fixed Nunito Black cells: the θ chip holds 105.5 px through every 2-digit value and 122.0 px through every 3-digit value, and a heat-map of f446-470 shows change only in the digit cells.
tests_run: Sprites on GPU 7 (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7), 3 runs, about 13 s each. Measured the shadow alpha at the sprite edges and fixed a 17% HDRI-occlusion leak by switching to a light-path world. Final edge alpha is at most 3.6% and is faded to 0 when loaded. A full re-run from scratch reproduces the assets to within 1/255 in the overlays (GPU rendering is not bit-exact).

make_overlays.py, all 900 frames in 7-10 s; 653 frames have content. The built-in self-test passes: nothing visible on 239/240, 419/420, 599/600 or 779/780; formula checkpoints θ(150)=90, θ(195)=360, θ(225)=405, τ(31)=0.92, τ(85)=1.28, τ(91)=1.40, zoom(105)=46.15; digit positions fixed for every value with the same digit count; no numbers in captions.

Cross-checked the builders' meta files against the storyboard formulas over every frame: theta_deg and tilt_deg within 1e-4; tau_s and rate within 1e-6; S04 zoom within 0.01 (the S04 meta uses its measured d0 = 8.0743 m).
Determinism: a single-process subset render (frames 61, 140, 230, 451, 515, 650, 706) is byte-identical to the parallel full run.

Visual review at 1:1 and 3x: pill and chip edges, the synthetic θ glyph, 3-slice joins, dot shadows, the white dot splitting into coral/lime/blue at f61-65, the chip reveal at 451-453 and shrink at 510-518, pill pop-in f121-130 (0.47, 0.79, 0.98, 1.06, 1.08, 1.055, 1.02, 1.0), pop-out f232-239 (gone at 238), and the strip pop anchored at its top-right corner.

Strip against the real S01 renders: the playhead falls between pink and violet at θ=90 (f150), and between orange and pink at θ=46 (f141) and θ=405 (f225). This matches R = Rz(-θ)·Ry(-φ) and the lead's calibration. The tilt visibly warps the horizon at f230.

Pulled frames 150 and 710 back out of the encoded captioned and clean MP4s: overlays sit correctly on the captioned film and are absent from the clean film.
Colour-matrix test on palette swatches decoded as a BT.709 player would: the make_mp4.sh filter chain is off by up to 21/255 per channel; the assemble.py chain is within 2/255.

qa_diff.py: pair (an identical pair gives 0.000, PASS), range on renders/film_comp and on renders/overlays with --prefix o_ (heat-map plus CSV), check presets (missing frames give exit 2 with a list), and crop scaling on 960x540 previews.
known_issues: scripts/make_mp4.sh (the lead's file; I left it alone) converts RGB to YUV with swscale's default BT.601 matrix and writes no colour tags. Players that assume BT.709 for HD shift palette pink and mint by up to 21/255. assemble.py does not use it: its encode chain adds out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv and bt709 tags. Suggest the lead apply the same two changes to make_mp4.sh for the builders' review MP4s.

Deviations from the storyboard, all visual tuning, logged in the script headers: chip pop-ins staggered +2 f (S01 chips start at f22 and f123); the strip starts at f125 instead of f121 (a cascade after the pill); chip widths spring to new content (overshoot when growing, ease without undershoot when shrinking); caption '·' separators at 45% ink and chip words at 62% ink; θ built from Nunito Black '0' plus a crossbar, because no project font contains θ; the slug is white at 60% over the S01 night phase, then cross-fades to ink; the sprite capsule is flattened to 62% depth; dots are lit more from overhead with a radial shadow fade; baked shadows are tinted ink instead of black.

Follows the spec, but worth knowing: the 'θ 405° · tilt ±4°' chip state exists only for f226-238 and pops out at 234-238, so it is fully readable for about 0.27 s. The ±4 is the amplitude round(max|tilt_deg|) taken from meta, not a live signed value, as the storyboard text specifies.
At f451-452 the S03 chip shows a partly revealed '0.2× · fran…' for 1-2 frames while it grows. This is the intended soft reveal.
qa_diff check s03-static needs --crop for the static stripe and block region, which depends on the S03 framing. Without it the whole frame is measured, gummy included.

assemble.py rewrites renders/film/, renders/film_comp/ and renders/film_comp_clean/ on every run, in both modes; out/ keeps final and preview apart, and out/[preview/]assembly.json records which mode built them. A preview run uses about 1.1 GB of 16-bit PNGs in film_comp_clean; in final mode, sources that are already 1920x1080 16-bit RGB are symlinked rather than copied.
The ProRes masters carry bt709 primaries, transfer and matrix but no range tag: prores_ks does not write one, and ProRes is video range by definition.
GPU sprite renders are not bit-exact from run to run (at most 1/255 in the overlays). Re-rendering the sprites does not visibly change anything.
